subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Zenwell
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Zenwell Eval Team <evals@zenwellhealth.com>, Zenwell Procurement <procurement@zenwellhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Zenwell

Hi Kevin / Zenwell team,

Thanks again for your time today — appreciate the candid discussion and the clarity on priorities. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of goals / decision criteria you called out:
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for typical 512-token prompts (priority)
- Stability: no more than 1% error/timeout rate during peak testing windows
- Cost: target blended cost-per-response that’s ~30% better than their current managed offering
- Instrumentation & compliance: token-level tracing, audit logs, and SOC 2 controls for PHI workflows

Top pain points you described:
- Current provider’s cold-start latency spikes during concurrent bursts
- Lack of consistent profiling across environments (dev/staging/prod)
- Limited caching/in-context reuse support which increases per-request compute

Competitive notes (from call + what we observed during trial):
- Competitor A: good raw throughput but opaque performance profiles; no easy canary rollouts
- Competitor B: strong for embeddings but higher token cost and limited KV cache features
- Redwood: unified routing (canary/fallback), prefix/KV caching, and transparent cost/latency dashboards — we think this lines up with your decision criteria.

Proposed bake-off plan / tests we agreed on:
1) Latency test: run 3 x 30-minute sustained concurrency windows (50 / 100 / 200 concurrent requests) using your sample dataset. Measure p50/p95/p99 and record error rates.
2) Cost simulation: replay the same traffic to capture per-token cost and overall monthly cost projection with expected query mix.
3) Stability test: sustained 8-hour soak test during a weekday window you pick.
4) Functional checks: tool-calling + structured output validation on 5 canonical prompts you provided.

What Redwood will deliver this week:
- Shared bakeoff matrix (attached) and the test harness (Drive link in this thread).
- Two trial API keys scoped to the evaluation project (one for testing, one for integration).
- A short checklist for test setup (included in the Drive folder).

What we need from Zenwell:
- Confirm target windows for the latency & soak tests (suggest Wed 3/17 for latency, Thu 3/18 for soak).
- Provide an access-controlled S3 or Drive location with the ~1k sample prompts (you already shared a sample; upload the full set).
- Point person for technical validation (Kevin — confirmed during call).

Attachments: bakeoff-matrix-zenwell.xlsx, zenwell-test-data-sample.csv

Next steps / owners:
- Aditya: coordinate scheduling + provide trial keys (I’ll send by EOD tomorrow).
- Jordan: set up the test harness and be on standby for any infra/questions.
- Marissa: prepare initial pricing framework and list of contract items to speed procurement.
- Kevin / Zenwell: confirm windows and upload test dataset.

If that lines up, I’ll lock the schedule and share the keys.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

---

Attachment: zenwell-test-data-sample.csv (csv)

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Zenwell

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Timeline: we prefer the latency windows the week of 3/22 but can run an initial quick latency check next Wed 3/17 if you need a fast read.
- Soak test: we want the 8-hour window to include a burst at hour 2 to simulate peak traffic (we’ll provide the burst profile).
- Data: I’ll upload the full 1k prompt set to the Drive folder you shared by EOD Friday (3/12).
- Security: procurement will need the SOC 2 report and our standard DPA redlines before we escalate to procurement. Marissa — can you share a high-level redline summary so we know which clauses to expect?

Also, one more success metric: quality parity — we’ll run a small eval set (50 prompts) and compare output accuracy / hallucination rates across vendors. Can Redwood provide a simple scoring script we can run locally?

Thanks —
Kevin Morales
Director, Platform Engineering
Zenwell Health
kevin.morales@zenwellhealth.com

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Zenwell

Thanks — quick notes from pricing/procurement side: 
- I’ll draft a one-page pricing framework (usage bands + reserved capacity options) and attach a sample SOW for the bake-off.
- We can offer a trial credit for the initial soak window to reduce risk — I’ll propose $5k credit in the SOW.
- Regarding the DPA/SOC2: legal can share a clean SOC 2 report and a redline summary by Monday 3/15.

Jordan: can you confirm the test harness has a scoring script for the 50-prompt quality check Kevin requested? If not, we should slot a 30-min sync early next week.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Zenwell

Kevin — perfect, appreciate the quick confirmations. Plan below and I’ll action items today: 

1) Keys + harness: I’ll send two scoped API keys and a link to the test harness by EOD today. Jordan will share the scoring script for the 50-prompt quality check.
2) Drive: Marissa — Kevin will upload full prompt set by EOD Friday (3/12) per Kevin’s note; once uploaded Jordan will kick off the latency window.
3) Schedule: we’ll hold the detailed latency windows the week of 3/22 as Kevin prefers; Jordan will propose specific 3-hour windows for each concurrency band by Tue 3/16.
4) Legal: Marissa to share SOC2 + redline summary on Monday 3/15. Procurement can review and confirm.
5) Credits: Marissa will include the $5k trial credit in the SOW.

If everyone’s aligned I’ll lock the HubSpot milestone and send calendar invites for the kickoff + tech runbooks.

Thanks all — looking forward to the tests.
